scope: Leviticus 8–10, all 80 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew numbering align throughout Leviticus 8–10. The full original XML record at 9:22 includes both the written hand and read hands forms.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Keeps the divine speech formula before the installation commands.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD spoke to Moses:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Retains people, garments, oil, bull, exactly two rams and bread basket in source order.
verses.before: “Take Aaron and his sons with him, the garments, the anointing oil, the bull of the sin offering, the two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread,
verses.after: “Bring Aaron and his sons with him, the garments and anointing oil, the bull for the sin offering, the two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Take Aaron and his sons with him, the garments, the anointing oil, the bull of the sin offering, the two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread,

verses.rationale: Keeps whole-community scope and the specified meeting place rather than narrowing to priests.
verses.before: and assemble the whole congregation at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.”
verses.after: Gather the whole community at the entrance of the tent of meeting.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and assemble the whole congregation at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.”

verses.rationale: Preserves obedience formula and repeated gathering location.
verses.before: Moses did as the LORD commanded him, and the congregation assembled at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
verses.after: Moses did as the LORD commanded him, and the community gathered at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses did as the LORD commanded him, and the congregation assembled at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

verses.rationale: Keeps public explanation and divine authority, with us supplying the natural object of the collective action.
verses.before: Moses said to the congregation, “This is what the LORD has commanded to be done.”
verses.after: Moses told the community, “This is what the LORD has commanded us to do.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses said to the congregation, “This is what the LORD has commanded to be done.”

verses.rationale: Retains Moses as washing agent and both Aaron and sons as recipients.
verses.before: Moses brought Aaron and his sons near and washed them with water.
verses.after: Then Moses brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses brought Aaron and his sons near and washed them with water.

verses.rationale: Keeps tunic, sash, robe, ephod and its distinct waistband, naming Aaron to clarify singular pronoun.
verses.before: He put the tunic on Aaron, tied the sash around him, clothed him with the robe, put the ephod on him, and fastened the skillfully woven band of the ephod around him.
verses.after: He put the tunic on Aaron, tied the sash around him, and dressed him in the robe. Then he put the ephod on him and secured it with its woven waistband.
verses.tsw_comparator: He put the tunic on Aaron, tied the sash around him, clothed him with the robe, put the ephod on him, and fastened the skillfully woven band of the ephod around him.

verses.rationale: Retains breastpiece and both named objects without assigning an unsupported mechanism.
verses.before: He placed the breastpiece on him and put the Urim and the Thummim into the breastpiece.
verses.after: He placed the breastpiece on him and put the Urim and Thummim inside it.
verses.tsw_comparator: He placed the breastpiece on him and put the Urim and the Thummim into the breastpiece.

verses.rationale: Keeps turban, front placement, gold plate and crown apposition with full command refrain.
verses.before: He set the turban on his head and placed the gold plate, the holy crown, on the front of the turban, as the LORD commanded Moses.
verses.after: He set the turban on Aaron’s head and attached the gold plate, the holy crown, to its front, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: He set the turban on his head and placed the gold plate, the holy crown, on the front of the turban, as the LORD commanded Moses.

verses.rationale: Preserves anointing of tent and contents and its consecrating purpose.
verses.before: Moses took the anointing oil and anointed the tabernacle and everything in it, making them holy.
verses.after: Moses took the anointing oil and anointed the tabernacle and everything in it, consecrating them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses took the anointing oil and anointed the tabernacle and everything in it, making them holy.

verses.rationale: Retains exact seven sprinklings and all named furnishings, distinct from Aaron’s poured oil.
verses.before: He sprinkled some of it on the altar seven times and anointed the altar and all its utensils, and the basin and its stand, to make them holy.
verses.after: He sprinkled some oil on the altar seven times, then anointed the altar and all its utensils, the basin and its stand, to consecrate them.
verses.tsw_comparator: He sprinkled some of it on the altar seven times and anointed the altar and all its utensils, and the basin and its stand, to make them holy.

verses.rationale: Keeps pour/anoint actions and repeated consecration without replacing with a generic appointment.
verses.before: He poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head and anointed him to make him holy.
verses.after: He poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head and anointed him to consecrate him.
verses.tsw_comparator: He poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head and anointed him to make him holy.

verses.rationale: Preserves sons’ three garments distinct from Aaron’s attire and repeats full command formula.
verses.before: Then Moses brought Aaron’s sons near, clothed them with tunics, tied sashes around them, and bound headbands on them, as the LORD commanded Moses.
verses.after: Moses brought Aaron’s sons forward, dressed them in tunics, tied sashes around them, and put head coverings on them, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Moses brought Aaron’s sons near, clothed them with tunics, tied sashes around them, and bound headbands on them, as the LORD commanded Moses.

verses.rationale: Keeps bull’s category and plural hand-laying by Aaron and sons.
verses.before: Moses brought forward the bull of the sin offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the head of the bull of the sin offering.
verses.after: He brought forward the bull for the sin offering. Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses brought forward the bull of the sin offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the head of the bull of the sin offering.

verses.rationale: Uses passive for unnamed slaughterer, preserves Moses’ finger/horns/base actions, and interprets atonement on altar with alternative for altar noted.
verses.before: Moses slaughtered it, took the blood, and with his finger put it on the horns of the altar on all sides, purifying the altar. He poured the blood at the base of the altar and made it holy, making atonement for it.
verses.after: The bull was slaughtered, and Moses took the blood. With his finger he put some on the altar’s horns all around, purifying the altar. He poured the remaining blood at its base and consecrated it so that atonement could be made on it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses slaughtered it, took the blood, and with his finger put it on the horns of the altar on all sides, purifying the altar. He poured the blood at the base of the altar and made it holy, making atonement for it.

verses.rationale: Preserves full anatomy, leaves the collection agent unassigned, and retains explicit Moses subject in altar action.
verses.before: Moses took all the fat around the entrails, the appendage of the liver, and the two kidneys with their fat, and turned them into smoke on the altar.
verses.after: All the fat on the entrails, the lobe of the liver, and both kidneys with their fat were taken, and Moses burned them on the altar as smoke.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses took all the fat around the entrails, the appendage of the liver, and the two kidneys with their fat, and turned them into smoke on the altar.

verses.rationale: Retains carcass contents, real disposal outside camp and command refrain, distinct from altar burning.
verses.before: But the bull, its skin, its flesh, and its dung he burned with fire outside the camp, as the LORD commanded Moses.
verses.after: But the bull—its skin, flesh, and dung—was burned with fire outside the camp, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the bull, its skin, its flesh, and its dung he burned with fire outside the camp, as the LORD commanded Moses.

verses.rationale: Keeps first ram’s category and repeated family hand-laying.
verses.before: He brought forward the ram of the burnt offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the ram’s head.
verses.after: He brought forward the ram for the burnt offering. Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.
verses.tsw_comparator: He brought forward the ram of the burnt offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the ram’s head.

verses.rationale: Leaves unnamed slaughterer unassigned and preserves named Moses’ splashing, not sprinkling.
verses.before: Moses slaughtered it and dashed the blood against all sides of the altar.
verses.after: The ram was slaughtered, and Moses splashed its blood against all sides of the altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses slaughtered it and dashed the blood against all sides of the altar.

verses.rationale: Preserves partitioning and three named items, identifying altar action without adding new anatomy.
verses.before: He cut the ram into its pieces, and Moses turned the head, the pieces, and the fat into smoke.
verses.after: The ram was cut into pieces, and Moses burned the head, the pieces, and the fat on the altar as smoke.
verses.tsw_comparator: He cut the ram into its pieces, and Moses turned the head, the pieces, and the fat into smoke.

verses.rationale: Keeps washing, whole-ram scope, three offering descriptions and full command refrain.
verses.before: He washed the entrails and legs with water, and Moses turned the entire ram into smoke on the altar. It was a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the LORD, as the LORD commanded Moses.
verses.after: The entrails and legs were washed with water, and Moses burned the whole ram on the altar as smoke. It was a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: He washed the entrails and legs with water, and Moses turned the entire ram into smoke on the altar. It was a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the LORD, as the LORD commanded Moses.

verses.rationale: Retains second ram and distinct ordination category, connecting filling-hands idiom in note.
verses.before: Then he brought forward the second ram, the ram of ordination, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the ram’s head.
verses.after: Then he brought forward the second ram, the ram for ordination. Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he brought forward the second ram, the ram of ordination, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the ram’s head.

verses.rationale: Keeps all three right-side body sites and partial blood quantity, without replacing rite with symbolic explanation.
verses.before: Moses slaughtered it and took some of its blood and put it on the lobe of Aaron’s right ear, the thumb of his right hand, and the big toe of his right foot.
verses.after: The ram was slaughtered, and Moses took some of its blood and put it on Aaron’s right earlobe, his right thumb, and the big toe of his right foot.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses slaughtered it and took some of its blood and put it on the lobe of Aaron’s right ear, the thumb of his right hand, and the big toe of his right foot.

verses.rationale: Repeats all three sites for the sons and distinguishes bodily application from altar splashing.
verses.before: He brought Aaron’s sons near, and Moses put some of the blood on the lobes of their right ears, the thumbs of their right hands, and the big toes of their right feet. Then Moses dashed the blood against all sides of the altar.
verses.after: He brought Aaron’s sons forward, and Moses put some blood on their right earlobes, their right thumbs, and the big toes of their right feet. Then Moses splashed the blood against all sides of the altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: He brought Aaron’s sons near, and Moses put some of the blood on the lobes of their right ears, the thumbs of their right hands, and the big toes of their right feet. Then Moses dashed the blood against all sides of the altar.

verses.rationale: Preserves full anatomy and right thigh, keeping tail as part of fat inventory.
verses.before: He took the fat, the fat tail, all the fat around the entrails, the appendage of the liver, the two kidneys with their fat, and the right thigh.
verses.after: He took the fat—the fat tail, all the fat on the entrails, the lobe of the liver, both kidneys with their fat—and the right thigh.
verses.tsw_comparator: He took the fat, the fat tail, all the fat around the entrails, the appendage of the liver, the two kidneys with their fat, and the right thigh.

verses.rationale: Keeps one of each of three bread forms, basket location and placement on both fat and thigh.
verses.before: From the basket of unleavened bread before the LORD he took one unleavened cake, one cake of bread made with oil, and one wafer, and placed them on the fat and the right thigh.
verses.after: From the basket of unleavened bread before the LORD, he took one unleavened cake, one cake made with oil, and one wafer, and placed them on the fat and right thigh.
verses.tsw_comparator: From the basket of unleavened bread before the LORD he took one unleavened cake, one cake of bread made with oil, and one wafer, and placed them on the fat and the right thigh.

verses.rationale: Preserves physical hands, all items and wave rite with the disputed waving agent left unassigned, and terminology consistent with Exodus 29.
verses.before: He placed all these in the hands of Aaron and his sons, and they elevated them as an elevation offering before the LORD.
verses.after: He placed all of these in Aaron’s hands and his sons’ hands. Then they were waved as a wave offering before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: He placed all these in the hands of Aaron and his sons, and they elevated them as an elevation offering before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps transfer from hands, placement on earlier offering and plural ordination designation with aroma/fire language.
verses.before: Then Moses took them from their hands and turned them into smoke on the altar on top of the burnt offering. They were an ordination offering, a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the LORD.
verses.after: Moses took them from their hands and burned them on the altar as smoke, on top of the burnt offering. They were ordination offerings, a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Moses took them from their hands and turned them into smoke on the altar on top of the burnt offering. They were an ordination offering, a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves breast specifically allocated to Moses and full command refrain rather than importing Aaron’s ordinary share.
verses.before: Moses took the breast and elevated it as an elevation offering before the LORD. It was Moses’ portion from the ram of ordination, as the LORD commanded Moses.
verses.after: Moses took the breast and waved it as a wave offering before the LORD. It was Moses’ share of the ordination ram, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses took the breast and elevated it as an elevation offering before the LORD. It was Moses’ portion from the ram of ordination, as the LORD commanded Moses.

verses.rationale: Retains oil and altar blood and full repeated people/garments list, distinguishing sprinkling from earlier pouring.
verses.before: Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood that was on the altar and sprinkled it on Aaron and his garments, and on his sons and their garments. So he made Aaron and his garments holy, and his sons and their garments with him.
verses.after: Moses took some anointing oil and some blood from the altar and sprinkled Aaron and his garments, his sons and their garments. In this way he consecrated Aaron and his garments, his sons and their garments.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood that was on the altar and sprinkled it on Aaron and his garments, and on his sons and their garments. So he made Aaron and his garments holy, and his sons and their garments with him.

verses.rationale: Keeps boiling and eating location, basket and source first-person I-commanded inside Moses’ speech.
verses.before: Moses said to Aaron and his sons, “Boil the flesh at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, and eat it there with the bread that is in the basket of ordination, as I commanded, saying, ‘Aaron and his sons will eat it.’
verses.after: Moses told Aaron and his sons, “Boil the meat at the entrance of the tent of meeting. Eat it there with the bread in the ordination basket, as I commanded when I said, ‘Aaron and his sons are to eat it.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses said to Aaron and his sons, “Boil the flesh at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, and eat it there with the bread that is in the basket of ordination, as I commanded, saying, ‘Aaron and his sons shall eat it.’

verses.rationale: Preserves both leftover categories and explicit burning command.
verses.before: What remains of the flesh and bread you will burn with fire.
verses.after: Burn whatever meat and bread remain.
verses.tsw_comparator: What remains of the flesh and bread you shall burn with fire.

verses.rationale: Preserves location restriction, repeated exact seven days and fulfillment language, with filling-hands idiom explained selectively.
verses.before: You will not go outside the entrance of the Tent of Meeting for seven days, until the days of your ordination are completed, for seven days will be used to ordain you.
verses.after: Do not leave the entrance of the tent of meeting for seven days, until your days of ordination are complete, for your ordination takes seven days.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not go outside the entrance of the Tent of Meeting for seven days, until the days of your ordination are completed, for seven days shall be used to ordain you.

verses.rationale: Keeps current-day action, divine command and atonement for priests, using passive for unexpressed agent.
verses.before: What has been done today, the LORD commanded to be done to make atonement for you.
verses.after: What has been done today is what the LORD commanded to be done to make atonement for you.
verses.tsw_comparator: What has been done today, the LORD commanded to be done to make atonement for you.

verses.rationale: Retains day/night residence, third seven-day statement, charge and death warning without softening consequence.
verses.before: You will remain at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting day and night for seven days and keep the LORD’s charge, so that you do not die, for so I have been commanded.”
verses.after: Stay at the entrance of the tent of meeting day and night for seven days. Keep the LORD’s charge so that you do not die, for this is what I was commanded.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall remain at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting day and night for seven days and keep the LORD’s charge, so that you do not die, for so I have been commanded.”

verses.rationale: Keeps comprehensive obedience and Moses’ mediating role at narrative close.
verses.before: Aaron and his sons did all the things that the LORD commanded through Moses.
verses.after: Aaron and his sons did everything the LORD had commanded through Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: Aaron and his sons did all the things that the LORD commanded through Moses.

verses.rationale: Retains eighth-day transition after seven-day ordination and all three groups summoned.
verses.before: On the eighth day Moses called Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel.
verses.after: On the eighth day, Moses called Aaron, his sons, and the elders of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the eighth day Moses called Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps Aaron’s two animal categories and defect prohibition applying to both.
verses.before: He said to Aaron, “Take for yourself a bull calf for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering, both without defect, and present them before the LORD.
verses.after: He told Aaron, “Take a bull calf for your sin offering and a ram for your burnt offering, both without defect, and present them before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to Aaron, “Take for yourself a bull calf for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering, both without defect, and present them before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains nested instruction through Aaron, male goat and exact one-year qualification of calf and lamb.
verses.before: Speak to the Israelites, saying: Take a male goat for a sin offering, and a calf and a lamb, each a year old and without defect, for a burnt offering,
verses.after: Tell the Israelites, ‘Take a male goat for a sin offering, and a calf and a lamb, both a year old and without defect, for a burnt offering,
verses.tsw_comparator: Speak to the Israelites, saying: Take a male goat for a sin offering, and a calf and a lamb, each a year old and without defect, for a burnt offering,

verses.rationale: Completes continuing list with ox/ram, grain/oil and same-day appearance promise to Israelites.
verses.before: and an ox and a ram for sacrifices of well-being to sacrifice before the LORD, and a grain offering mixed with oil, for today the LORD will appear to you.”
verses.after: an ox and a ram for peace offerings to sacrifice before the LORD, and a grain offering mixed with oil, for today the LORD will appear to you.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: and an ox and a ram for sacrifices of well-being to sacrifice before the LORD, and a grain offering mixed with oil, for today the LORD will appear to you.”

verses.rationale: Keeps commanded gifts, tent-front location, whole gathering and standing posture.
verses.before: They brought what Moses commanded before the Tent of Meeting. The whole congregation drew near and stood before the LORD.
verses.after: They brought what Moses had commanded to the front of the tent of meeting. The whole community came forward and stood before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: They brought what Moses commanded before the Tent of Meeting. The whole congregation drew near and stood before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Unfolds command/result syntax without deleting glory or repeated divine name.
verses.before: Moses said, “This is what the LORD has commanded you to do, so that the glory of the LORD may appear to you.”
verses.after: Moses said, “Do what the LORD has commanded, and the LORD’s glory will appear to you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses said, “This is what the LORD has commanded you to do, so that the glory of the LORD may appear to you.”

verses.rationale: Preserves atonement for people in both clauses rather than correcting first occurrence to household.
verses.before: Then Moses said to Aaron, “Draw near to the altar and prepare your sin offering and your burnt offering, making atonement for yourself and for the people. Then prepare the people’s offering and make atonement for them, as the LORD commanded.”
verses.after: Then Moses told Aaron, “Approach the altar and present your sin offering and burnt offering, making atonement for yourself and the people. Then present the people’s offering and make atonement for them, as the LORD commanded.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Moses said to Aaron, “Draw near to the altar and prepare your sin offering and your burnt offering, making atonement for yourself and for the people. Then prepare the people’s offering and make atonement for them, as the LORD commanded.”

verses.rationale: Retains Aaron’s explicit slaughter and his own offering distinct from people’s later goat.
verses.before: Aaron drew near to the altar and slaughtered the calf of the sin offering that was for himself.
verses.after: Aaron approached the altar and slaughtered the calf for his own sin offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: Aaron drew near to the altar and slaughtered the calf of the sin offering that was for himself.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes sons’ delivery from Aaron’s finger/horns/base actions.
verses.before: Aaron’s sons brought the blood to him. He dipped his finger in the blood, put it on the horns of the altar, and poured the blood at the base of the altar.
verses.after: Aaron’s sons brought him the blood. He dipped his finger in it, put some on the altar’s horns, and poured the rest at the altar’s base.
verses.tsw_comparator: Aaron’s sons brought the blood to him. He dipped his finger in the blood, put it on the horns of the altar, and poured the blood at the base of the altar.

verses.rationale: Retains all named parts and Moses-command refrain without inventing tail for calf.
verses.before: He turned the fat, the kidneys, and the appendage of the liver from the sin offering into smoke on the altar, as the LORD commanded Moses.
verses.after: He burned the sin offering’s fat, kidneys, and lobe of the liver on the altar as smoke, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: He turned the fat, the kidneys, and the appendage of the liver from the sin offering into smoke on the altar, as the LORD commanded Moses.

verses.rationale: Keeps both carcass materials and outside-camp burning, distinct from altar offering.
verses.before: The flesh and skin he burned with fire outside the camp.
verses.after: He burned the flesh and skin with fire outside the camp.
verses.tsw_comparator: The flesh and skin he burned with fire outside the camp.

verses.rationale: Keeps Aaron slaughter, sons delivery and circumferential splashing distinct from finger application.
verses.before: Then he slaughtered the burnt offering. Aaron’s sons handed the blood to him, and he dashed it against all sides of the altar.
verses.after: Then he slaughtered the burnt offering. Aaron’s sons handed him the blood, and he splashed it against all sides of the altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he slaughtered the burnt offering. Aaron’s sons handed the blood to him, and he dashed it against all sides of the altar.

verses.rationale: Preserves successive transfer of pieces and separate head, with Aaron remaining altar agent.
verses.before: They handed him the burnt offering piece by piece, together with the head, and he turned them into smoke on the altar.
verses.after: They handed him the burnt offering piece by piece, together with the head, and he burned them on the altar as smoke.
verses.tsw_comparator: They handed him the burnt offering piece by piece, together with the head, and he turned them into smoke on the altar.

verses.rationale: Keeps washing and placement atop other offering parts without adding water absent in this verse.
verses.before: He washed the entrails and legs and turned them into smoke with the burnt offering on the altar.
verses.after: He washed the entrails and legs and burned them on top of the burnt offering on the altar as smoke.
verses.tsw_comparator: He washed the entrails and legs and turned them into smoke with the burnt offering on the altar.

verses.rationale: Retains people’s distinct goat and comparison with prior calf without forcing every disposal detail identical.
verses.before: Then Aaron presented the people’s offering. He took the goat of the sin offering for the people, slaughtered it, and offered it for sin like the first.
verses.after: Next he brought forward the people’s offering. He took their goat for the sin offering, slaughtered it, and presented it as a sin offering just as he had the first one.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Aaron presented the people’s offering. He took the goat of the sin offering for the people, slaughtered it, and offered it for sin like the first.

verses.rationale: Keeps offering category and procedural standard without importing unexpressed details.
verses.before: He presented the burnt offering and prepared it according to the ordinance.
verses.after: He brought forward the burnt offering and prepared it according to the prescribed rule.
verses.tsw_comparator: He presented the burnt offering and prepared it according to the ordinance.

verses.rationale: Preserves handful and additive relation to morning offering, not replacing daily service.
verses.before: He presented the grain offering, filled his hand from it, and turned it into smoke on the altar, in addition to the morning burnt offering.
verses.after: He brought forward the grain offering, took a handful of it, and burned it on the altar as smoke, in addition to the morning burnt offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: He presented the grain offering, filled his hand from it, and turned it into smoke on the altar, in addition to the morning burnt offering.

verses.rationale: Keeps both animals and repeated sons/Aaron blood-action distinction.
verses.before: Then he slaughtered the ox and the ram, the sacrifice of well-being for the people. Aaron’s sons handed the blood to him, and he dashed it against all sides of the altar.
verses.after: He slaughtered the ox and ram as the people’s peace offerings. Aaron’s sons handed him the blood, and he splashed it against all sides of the altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he slaughtered the ox and the ram, the sacrifice of well-being for the people. Aaron’s sons handed the blood to him, and he dashed it against all sides of the altar.

verses.rationale: Keeps combined fat inventory with tail naturally belonging to ram, carrying list into placement verse without attributing tail to ox.
verses.before: They also handed him the fat of the ox and ram—the fat tail, the fat covering the entrails, the kidneys, and the appendage of the liver.
verses.after: As for the fat portions from the ox and ram—the fat tail, the fat covering the entrails, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver—
verses.tsw_comparator: They also handed him the fat of the ox and ram—the fat tail, the fat covering the entrails, the kidneys, and the appendage of the liver.

verses.rationale: Preserves plural sons’ placement, breasts as support and singular Aaron’s fat burning.
verses.before: They placed the fat portions on the breasts, and he turned the fat into smoke on the altar.
verses.after: they placed the fat portions on the breasts, and Aaron burned the fat portions on the altar as smoke.
verses.tsw_comparator: They placed the fat portions on the breasts, and he turned the fat into smoke on the altar.

verses.rationale: Retains plural breasts and source singular thigh, named Aaron and command by Moses without adding LORD absent here.
verses.before: Aaron elevated the breasts and the right thigh as an elevation offering before the LORD, as Moses commanded.
verses.after: Aaron waved the breasts and right thigh as a wave offering before the LORD, as Moses had commanded.
verses.tsw_comparator: Aaron elevated the breasts and the right thigh as an elevation offering before the LORD, as Moses commanded.

verses.rationale: Follows qere hands over written singular hand, retains direction, blessing and all three completed offering categories.
verses.before: Aaron lifted his hands toward the people and blessed them. Then he came down after preparing the sin offering, the burnt offering, and the sacrifices of well-being.
verses.after: Aaron lifted his hands toward the people and blessed them. Then he came down after presenting the sin offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offerings.
verses.tsw_comparator: Aaron lifted his hands toward the people and blessed them. Then he came down after preparing the sin offering, the burnt offering, and the sacrifices of well-being.

verses.rationale: Preserves both entrants, exit, shared blessing and glory visible to all without inventing activity inside tent.
verses.before: Moses and Aaron entered the Tent of Meeting. When they came out, they blessed the people, and the glory of the LORD appeared to all the people.
verses.after: Moses and Aaron went into the tent of meeting. When they came out, they blessed the people, and the LORD’s glory appeared to all the people.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses and Aaron entered the Tent of Meeting. When they came out, they blessed the people, and the glory of the LORD appeared to all the people.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine-origin fire and consuming action, all-people response and physical prostration, linking same verbs to 10:2.
verses.before: Fire came out from before the LORD and consumed the burnt offering and the fat portions on the altar. When all the people saw it, they shouted and fell on their faces.
verses.after: Fire came out from before the LORD and consumed the burnt offering and fat on the altar. All the people saw it, shouted, and fell facedown.
verses.tsw_comparator: Fire came out from before the LORD and consumed the burnt offering and the fat portions on the altar. When all the people saw it, they shouted and fell on their faces.

verses.rationale: Keeps each son’s own vessel, fire/incense sequence and uncommanded offering; foreign-fire ambiguity noted without inventing intoxication.
verses.before: Nadab and Abihu, sons of Aaron, each took his firepan, put fire in it, placed incense on it, and brought unauthorized fire before the LORD, which the LORD had not commanded them.
verses.after: Aaron’s sons Nadab and Abihu each took his firepan, put fire in it, and laid incense on it. They presented unauthorized fire before the LORD, which he had not commanded them to offer.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nadab and Abihu, sons of Aaron, each took his firepan, put fire in it, placed incense on it, and brought unauthorized fire before the LORD, which the LORD had not commanded them.

verses.rationale: Preserves same consuming-fire language as 9:24, explicit deaths and repeated divine presence without softening violence.
verses.before: Fire came out from before the LORD and consumed them, and they died before the LORD.
verses.after: Fire came out from before the LORD and consumed them, and they died before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Fire came out from before the LORD and consumed them, and they died before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves two parallel divine declarations within verse paragraph and Aaron’s silence without assigning him agreement or suppressed emotion.
verses.before: Then Moses said to Aaron, “This is what the LORD spoke, saying: ‘Among people who come near me, I will show myself holy, and before all the people I will be glorified.’” Aaron was silent.
verses.after: Moses said to Aaron, “This is what the LORD said: ‘Among those near me I will show myself holy; before all the people I will be honored.’” And Aaron was silent.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Moses said to Aaron, “This is what the LORD spoke, saying: ‘Among those who come near me, I will show myself holy, and before all the people I will be glorified.’” And Aaron was silent.

verses.rationale: Keeps all names, uncle relationship and relatives for kin-brothers, with sanctuary-front/outside movement.
verses.before: Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, sons of Uzziel, Aaron’s uncle, and said to them, “Come near and carry your relatives away from the front of the sanctuary to a place outside the camp.”
verses.after: Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Aaron’s uncle Uzziel. He told them, “Come forward and carry your relatives away from the front of the sanctuary to a place outside the camp.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, sons of Uzziel, Aaron’s uncle, and said to them, “Come near and carry your relatives away from the front of the sanctuary to a place outside the camp.”

verses.rationale: Retains garments and obeyed removal without claiming bodies or clothes were reduced to ashes.
verses.before: So they came near and carried them in their tunics outside the camp, as Moses had said.
verses.after: They came forward and carried them outside the camp in their tunics, as Moses had said.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they came near and carried them in their tunics outside the camp, as Moses had said.

verses.rationale: Preserves named survivors, both mourning restrictions, death and communal wrath, while allowing wider Israel’s mourning and naming LORD as agent.
verses.before: Then Moses said to Aaron and to his sons Eleazar and Ithamar, “Do not let the hair of your heads go loose and do not tear your garments, so that you do not die and wrath does not come upon the whole congregation. But your relatives, the whole house of Israel, may mourn the burning that the LORD has kindled.
verses.after: Moses told Aaron and his sons Eleazar and Ithamar, “Do not let your hair hang loose or tear your clothes, so that you do not die and wrath does not fall on the whole community. But your relatives, the whole house of Israel, may mourn the burning the LORD has brought about.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Moses said to Aaron and to his sons Eleazar and Ithamar, “Do not let the hair of your heads go loose and do not tear your garments, so that you do not die and wrath does not come upon the whole congregation. But your relatives, the whole house of Israel, may mourn the burning that the LORD has kindled.

verses.rationale: Keeps location restriction, death risk and anointing reason, then returns to narrator for obedience.
verses.before: You will not go outside the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, or you will die, for the LORD’s anointing oil is upon you.” And they did according to the word of Moses.
verses.after: Do not leave the entrance of the tent of meeting, or you may die, because the LORD’s anointing oil is on you.” They did as Moses said.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not go outside the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, or you will die, for the LORD’s anointing oil is upon you.” And they did according to the word of Moses.

verses.rationale: Preserves direct address to Aaron, not mechanically replacing with Moses formula.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Aaron, saying,
verses.after: The LORD spoke to Aaron:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Aaron, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps addressees, both drink categories, entering-service context, death consequence and lasting scope without retroactively alleging sons’ drunkenness.
verses.before: “You and your sons with you will drink no wine or strong drink when you enter the Tent of Meeting, so that you do not die. This is a perpetual statute throughout your generations,
verses.after: “You and your sons with you must not drink wine or other intoxicating drink when you enter the tent of meeting, so that you do not die. This is a lasting statute throughout your generations.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You and your sons with you shall drink no wine or strong drink when you enter the Tent of Meeting, so that you do not die. This is a perpetual statute throughout your generations,

verses.rationale: Retains two separate category pairs and keeps sentence connected to teaching duty.
verses.before: so that you may distinguish between the holy and the common, and between the unclean and the clean,
verses.after: You must distinguish between the holy and the common, and between the unclean and the clean,
verses.tsw_comparator: so that you may distinguish between the holy and the common, and between the unclean and the clean,

verses.rationale: Completes coordinated priestly duty with Israelite recipients, all-statutes scope and Mosaic mediation.
verses.before: and so that you may teach the Israelites all the statutes that the LORD has spoken to them through Moses.”
verses.after: and teach the Israelites all the statutes the LORD has given them through Moses.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and so that you may teach the Israelites all the statutes that the LORD has spoken to them through Moses.”

verses.rationale: Keeps survivors named, remainder, unleavened preparation, altar-side eating and most-holy category.
verses.before: Moses spoke to Aaron and to Eleazar and Ithamar, his remaining sons: “Take the grain offering that remains from the offerings by fire to the LORD and eat it unleavened beside the altar, for it is most holy.
verses.after: Moses told Aaron and his surviving sons Eleazar and Ithamar, “Take the grain offering left from the LORD’s offerings by fire, and eat it without leaven beside the altar, because it is most holy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses spoke to Aaron and to Eleazar and Ithamar, his remaining sons: “Take the grain offering that remains from the offerings by fire to the LORD and eat it unleavened beside the altar, for it is most holy.

verses.rationale: Preserves holy-place rule, separate father/sons shares and Moses’ received command.
verses.before: You will eat it in a holy place, because it is your portion and your sons’ portion from the offerings by fire to the LORD, for so I have been commanded.
verses.after: Eat it in a holy place, for it is your share and your sons’ share of the LORD’s offerings by fire. This is what I was commanded.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall eat it in a holy place, because it is your portion and your sons’ portion from the offerings by fire to the LORD, for so I have been commanded.

verses.rationale: Retains clean versus holy place and explicit daughters permitted this food, without broadening earlier most-holy food rule.
verses.before: But the breast of the elevation offering and the thigh of the contribution you may eat in a clean place, you and your sons and daughters with you, for they are given as your portion and your children’s portion from the Israelites’ sacrifices of well-being.
verses.after: But you may eat the breast of the wave offering and the contributed thigh in a clean place, you and your sons and daughters with you. They have been given as your share and your sons’ share from the Israelites’ peace offerings.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the breast of the elevation offering and the thigh of the contribution you may eat in a clean place, you and your sons and daughters with you, for they are given as your portion and your children’s portion from the Israelites’ sacrifices of well-being.

verses.rationale: Preserves thigh/breast presentation with fat, wave rite and enduring family allocation.
verses.before: They will bring the thigh of the contribution and the breast of the elevation offering together with the fat portions offered by fire, to elevate them as an elevation offering before the LORD. They will belong to you and your children with you as a perpetual portion, as the LORD commanded.”
verses.after: The contributed thigh and the breast of the wave offering are to be brought with the fat portions offered by fire, to be waved before the LORD. They will be a lasting share for you and your sons with you, as the LORD commanded.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall bring the thigh of the contribution and the breast of the elevation offering together with the fat portions offered by fire, to elevate them as an elevation offering before the LORD. They shall belong to you and your children with you as a perpetual portion, as the LORD commanded.”

verses.rationale: Retains emphatic searching, discovery of burning, anger and repeated surviving-son designation.
verses.before: Moses carefully searched for the goat of the sin offering, and look—it had been burned. He became angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron’s remaining sons, saying,
verses.after: Moses searched carefully for the goat of the sin offering—and found that it had been burned. He was angry with Aaron’s surviving sons Eleazar and Ithamar and said,
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses carefully searched for the goat of the sin offering, and look—it had been burned. He became angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron’s remaining sons, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves Moses’ question, holiness, understood divine giver named for clarity and priests bearing communal guilt without collapsing to personal guilt.
verses.before: “Why did you not eat the sin offering in the holy place? It is most holy, and the LORD gave it to you to bear the guilt of the congregation, to make atonement for them before the LORD.
verses.after: “Why did you not eat the sin offering in the holy place? It is most holy, and the LORD gave it to you to bear the community’s guilt and make atonement for them before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Why did you not eat the sin offering in the holy place? It is most holy, and the LORD gave it to you to bear the guilt of the congregation, to make atonement for them before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps interior-blood exception’s absence and emphatic should-have-eaten, consistent with 6:30.
verses.before: Look, its blood was not brought inside the sanctuary. You certainly should have eaten it in the sanctuary, as I commanded.”
verses.after: Its blood was not brought inside the sanctuary. You should certainly have eaten it in a holy place, as I commanded!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, its blood was not brought inside the sanctuary. You certainly should have eaten it in the sanctuary, as I commanded.”

verses.rationale: Keeps unresolved they, Aaron’s first-person loss and rhetorical question about acceptable eating without adding a settled legal rationale.
verses.before: Aaron said to Moses, “Look, today they presented their sin offering and their burnt offering before the LORD, and such things as these have happened to me. If I had eaten the sin offering today, would it have been good in the eyes of the LORD?”
verses.after: Aaron answered Moses, “Today they presented their sin offering and burnt offering before the LORD, yet these things have happened to me. If I had eaten a sin offering today, would that have pleased the LORD?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Aaron said to Moses, “Look, today they presented their sin offering and their burnt offering before the LORD, and such things as these have happened to me. If I had eaten the sin offering today, would it have been good in the eyes of the LORD?”

verses.rationale: Preserves Moses’ favorable response and echo of pleasing in Aaron’s question without inventing a new command or rebuke.
verses.before: When Moses heard this, it was good in his eyes.
verses.after: When Moses heard this, he was satisfied.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Moses heard this, it was good in his eyes.
